Teaching and supervision
Since 2018, I have delivered more than 180 hours of teaching and supervised more than 10 students, from undergraduate to PhD level.

Co-supervision of four undergraduate final-year projects at UAM (2025–2026), on photon isolation in challenging environments and Higgs boson differential cross-section measurements with Run 3 data.
Laboratory sub-coordinator at UAM (2024–2025), coordinating first-year biology laboratory sessions (24 hours).
Laboratory teaching at UAM (2024–2025), physics laboratory sessions for third-year physics students (32 hours).
Supervision of four ATLAS qualification tasks (2022–2024), covering prompt electron and photon isolation and identification efficiencies.
Master Instructor for LA-CoNGA Physics (2021), teaching an introduction to data analysis with ATLAS Open Data (4 hours).
Teaching at Université de Paris (2018–2020), including elementary physics for first-year medicine students (36 hours) and computing courses for first-year science students (64 hours).

title: Research
text: My research focuses on experimental particle physics at the Large Hadron Collider, within the ATLAS Collaboration. I work at the interface between physics analyses and the development of experimental methods, combining searches for new phenomena with improvements in the reconstruction and identification of physics objects.

title: Research
text:
Current research topics

SoftDrop-based photon isolation
My PhD research focused on photon isolation in high-pile-up environments and searches for axion-like particles decaying into two photons. Since then, I have worked on electron and photon identification and isolation, efficiency measurements, and methods to estimate fake and non-prompt backgrounds in different analysis contexts. This work has also involved developing software and performance recommendations for use across the ATLAS Collaboration, as well as prospective studies for the High-Luminosity LHC.
At Universidad Autónoma de Madrid, I am developing and implementing SoftDrop-based techniques for photon isolation. This work investigates whether a substructure-based approach can improve photon isolation and its robustness in the challenging environments encountered at hadron colliders.


Searches for diphoton resonances in boosted topologies
I have contributed to ATLAS searches for additional scalar particles and exotic Higgs boson decays, including signatures with diphoton, photon–tau and collimated-lepton final states. My work has covered low- and high-mass resonance searches, as well as analyses targeting challenging boosted topologies.
I am involved in searches for diphoton resonances in highly boosted topologies, where the two photons can become increasingly collimated. These challenging signatures motivate the exploration of machine-learning techniques to improve signal identification and sensitivity to new-physics scenarios.


Higgs boson physics
I have contributed to Higgs boson measurements and searches with the ATLAS detector. This includes serving as analysis contact for the measurement of the differential Higgs boson production cross-section in the diphoton final state using partial Run 3 data collected through 2024.

title: Luis Pascual Domínguez
text:
Postdoctoral Research Fellow · Universidad Autónoma de Madd ATLAS Collaboration · CERN
I am an experimental particle physicist and I joined the ATLAS collaboration at the Large Hadron Collider in 2017 as a PhD student and I have been a qualified ATLAS author since 2018. My current research areas are focused on photon physics, Higgs boson measurements and searches for New Physics.
My research spans physics analyses and detector-level activities, with experience in photon and lepton reconstruction, identification and isolation, instrumental to improve our knowledge of Nature through the analysis of proton-proton collision at the LHC.

title: Luis Pascual Domínguez
text:
Main research interests

Higgs boson physics: measurements and searches involving rare and unconventional Higgs boson signatures.
Beyond the Standard Model: searches for additional scalar particles, low-mass resonances and collimated leptonic signatures.
Photon reconstruction, identification and isolation: photon reconstruction, identification and isolation performances in hadron colliders for particle physics analyses.
